question.text: A company sells two types of notebooks, A and B. Each notebook requires two processes: printing and binding. Notebook A requires $2$ minutes for printing and $1$ minute for binding. $2x + 4y \leq 360$

The time required for binding notebook A is $1$ minute and for notebook B is $2$ minutes. The maximum time available for binding is $2$ hours, which is $2 \times 60 = 120$ minutes. This gives the binding constraint:

$x + 2y \leq 120$

$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

Combining all these, the LPP is to maximize $z = 2x + 5y$ subject to $2x + 4y \leq 360$, $x + 2y \leq 120$, $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$.

solution.text: $\begin{array}{rlr} & (x \cdot y)+\left[\left(x+y^{\prime}\right) \cdot y\right]^{\prime} & \\ & =(x \cdot y)+\left[\left(x+y^{\prime}\right)^{\prime}+y^{\prime}\right] & {\left[\because(a \cdot b)^{\prime}=a^{\prime}+b^{\prime}\right]} \\ & =(x \cdot y)+\left[x^{\prime} \cdot\left(y^{\prime}\right)^{\prime}+y^{\prime}\right] & {\left[\because(a+b)^{\prime}=a^{\prime} \cdot b^{\prime}\right]} \\ & =(x \cdot y)+\left[x^{\prime} \cdot y+y^{\prime}\right] & {\left[\because\left(a^{\prime}\right)^{\prime}=a\right]} \\ & =x \cdot y+y^{\prime}+x^{\prime} \cdot y & {[\because a+b=b+a]} \\ & =x \cdot y+\left(y^{\prime}+x^{\prime}\right) \cdot\left(y^{\prime}+y\right)[\text { by distributive law }] \\ & =x \cdot y+\left(y^{\prime}+x^{\prime}\right) \cdot 1 & {\left[\because a+a^{\prime}=1\right]} \\ & =x \cdot y+x^{\prime}+y^{\prime} & \\ & =x \cdot y+(x \cdot y)^{\prime} & {\left[\because a^{\prime}+b^{\prime}=(a \cdot b)^{\prime}\right]} \\ & =1 & {\left[\because a+a^{\prime}=1\right]}\end{array}$
